facts.statement: Zephyrosaurus is a genus of orodromine ornithischian dinosaur known from a partial skull and postcranial fragments found in the Early Cretaceous Cloverly Formation of Montana.
facts.quote: Zephyrosaurus (meaning "westward wind lizard") is a genus of orodromine ornithischian dinosaur based on a partial skull and postcranial fragments discovered in the Early Cretaceous (Aptian-Albian) Cloverly Formation of Carbon County, Montana, USA.

facts.statement: Some bones of Zephyrosaurus may have allowed for movement within the skull, known as cranial kinesis.
facts.quote: Some of the bones may have allowed movement within the skull (cranial kinesis) as well.

facts.statement: Zephyrosaurus possessed beak teeth, a trait shared with other orodromines.
facts.quote: Like other orodromines, it had beak teeth.

facts.statement: Zephyrosaurus was approximately 1.8 meters long and weighed about 50 kilograms.
facts.quote: De solo 1,8 metros de longitud, llegaría a pesar 50 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Zephyrosaurus was a small, swift, bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Zephyrosaurus would have been a small, swift, bipedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Zephyrosaurus may have been capable of burrowing, similar to Orodromeus and Oryctodromeus.
facts.quote: Like Orodromeus and Oryctodromeus, it may have burrowed as well.

facts.statement: The fossil record of Zephyrosaurus spans from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type specimen MCZ 4392 consists of jaw fragments, the braincase, associated bones, partial vertebrae, and rib fragments.
facts.quote: MCZ 4392, the type specimen, is composed of jaw fragments, the braincase and associated bones, several partial vertebrae, and rib fragments.

facts.statement: Hans-Dieter Sues named the genus after finding it in the western United States, while C. R. Schaff was the one who found the specimen.
facts.quote: Hans-Dieter Sues quien descubriera al género lo nombró debido a que ha sido encontrado en el oeste de Estados Unidos, y C. R. Schaff, quien encontrara el espécimen.

facts.statement: In 2003, Martha Kutter reported new remains of Zephyrosaurus at the Sam Noble Oklahoma Museum of Natural History, including bones from at least seven individuals covering all body regions.
facts.quote: Martha Kutter, en un resumen de 2003, señaló sobre los restos nuevos de este género bajo estudio en Sam Noble Oklahoma Museum of Natural History, incluyendo los restos por lo menos de siete individuos con huesos de todas las regiones del cuerpo.

facts.statement: In 2004, Stanford et al. attributed dinosaur tracks named Hypsiloichnus marylandicus from Maryland and Virginia to an animal related to Zephyrosaurus based on hand and foot proportions.
facts.quote: Stanford et al. (2004) publicó un análisis de las huellas de dinosaurio de la Formación Patuxent de Maryland y de Virginia, a los cuales nombraron 'Hypsiloichnus marylandicus y atribuido a un animal relacionado al Zephyrosaurus basado en las proporciones de las manos y de los pies.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis in the 2010s classified Zephyrosaurus as a member of the Thescelosauridae family.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis in the 2010s has classified Zephyrosaurus as part of the Thescelosauridae family.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis in the 2010s classified Zephyrosaurus as part of the Thescelosauridae family.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético en la década de 2010 ha clasificado a Zephyrosaurus como parte de la familia Thescelosauridae.

facts.statement: Some studies have struggled to classify Zephyrosaurus due to the fragmentary nature of the original fossil material.
facts.quote: Other studies have had difficulty classifying it, due to the sparseness of the original material.

facts.statement: The original description suggested Zephyrosaurus represented a previously unknown lineage of hypsilophodonts, similar in some respects to Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: He found the new genus to represent a previously unknown lineage of hypsilophodont (a taxon now considered not natural), similar in some respects to Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: Fossil tracks from Maryland and Virginia have been attributed to Zephyrosaurus.
facts.quote: Rastros de icnitas Maryland y Virginia son atribuidas a este dinosaurio.

rejected.quote: Among other distinctive characteristics, it had a steep face, a raised knob on the upper jaw, and a larger knob on the cheekbone.
